items.title: Benny Golson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: That’s how I met him. ... Tony Bennett wanted to put words to a song I wrote called Sad to Say

ctx.x: That’s how I met him. He put words to my song. That should have been a falling out before it happened. You can’t do that, just put words to a person’s song and then record it, you don’t say anything. I supposed to think this is an honor? No. Tony Bennett wanted to put words to a song I wrote called Sad to Say, but he wanted to do something about Bill Evans. I said, “I’m sorry. That’s not what I had in mind.”
But at least he came to you to ask about it.
